justification: Assessment returned INVALID with first failing step 0005, and its point (c) targets exactly the ground-truth flaw: the claim that n+1's factors must lie among the previous n numbers so n+1 = prod n_i of strictly smaller factors. It notes this fails precisely for primes (giving n+1 = 17 and n+1 = 2 as witnesses), matching the ground-truth witness class (all primes; smallest 2, clean example 7). Reasoning is correct: for prime p the only divisors are 1 and p, so no multiset of factors in [2, p-1] has product p. Empty counterexample field is compensated by explicit witnesses in the reasoning.
